Parameter configs

Source: R/param_config.R
param_config.Rd

A config is a named list of params that defines all parameters of a pipeline.

Usage

param_config(..., .duplicates = c("error", "first"))

# S3 method for class 'param_config'
c(..., .duplicates = c("error", "first"))

# S3 method for class 'param_config'
x[i]

Arguments

...

Params (named arguments), lists of params or configs. NULL arguments are ignored. The names of list arguments are not used, only those of the params in them.

.duplicates

"error" (default) or "first": what to do with params of the same name.

x

A param config.

i

Index of the elements to keep.

Value

A named list of params with class c("param_config", "list").

Details

Functions

  • param_config() collects params into a config. It checks that all elements are params with unique names and numbers them (attribute order), which sets their order in the parameter UI.

  • c() combines configs (and further params or lists of params) and numbers the params anew.

  • [ selects params and keeps the class. Unknown names and indices are an error.

Duplicate names are an error, unless you set .duplicates = "first": then the first definition wins. This is useful to merge the configs of combined pipelines, where the more specific definition comes first (see Examples).

See also

param(), pub_get_params()

Examples

prep <- param_config(
    yUnit = param("%", label = "Unit of y"),
    alpha = numeric_param(0.05, label = "Alpha", min = 0, max = 1)
)
stats <- param_config(
    alpha = numeric_param(0.01, label = "Alpha", min = 0, max = 1),
    list(showPoints = param(TRUE, label = "Show points?"))
)
names(prep)
#> [1] "yUnit" "alpha"
param_attr(stats$showPoints, "order")
#> [1] 2

# Merge configs: the first definition of 'alpha' wins
full <- c(prep, stats, .duplicates = "first")
param_value(full$alpha)
#> [1] 0.05
vapply(full, param_attr, numeric(1), which = "order")
#>      yUnit      alpha showPoints 
#>          1          2          3 

# By default, duplicate names are an error
try(c(prep, stats))
#> Error in c(prep, stats) : Duplicate param names: alpha.
#> ℹ Use `.duplicates = "first"` to keep the first definition.
